audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may omit the reinvestment required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; latest FY2026 total-capex guidance is $240-$275 million, equal to 113%-130% of the $212.1 million OE anchor, but the growth-required portion is not disclosed
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth capital expenditures and incremental working capital should reduce forecast OE supporting the 3% base and 6% bull growth paths.
audit_findings.evidence: Total capital expenditures in fiscal 2026 are planned to be between approximately $250 million to $300 million and are expected to be funded primarily by cash generated from operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved but potentially material modeling error. The disclosed method compounds the anchor without showing a reinvestment charge, while planned total capital spending exceeds the entire OE anchor. Total capex cannot be treated wholly as growth investment, but the available record demonstrates enough scale for omitted growth reinvestment to change the base and bull values materially.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance from growth capex and quantify incremental inventory and other working capital for each growth scenario; rerun base and bull cash flows after deducting those investments.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat all cash as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum bridge exposure $320.614 million, or $2.96 per share and 9.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any minimum operating cash should be removed from the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary cash needs are for merchandise inventories, payroll, store rent, and other operating expenses and capital expenditures associated with opening new stores and remodeling existing stores as well as information technology, e-commerce, store support center, and distribution center infrastructure.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the full $320.614 million, but the amount actually required for operations is unresolved. Even excluding all cash—an intentionally conservative ceiling—would reduce base value from $30.42 to approximately $27.47 per share and bull value from $35.36 to approximately $32.41, both still well below the $50.23 market price. It therefore cannot reverse the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a minimum-cash analysis using payroll, rent, inventory purchasing, committed capex, letters of credit, seasonal cash troughs, and available revolver capacity; rerun the bridge using only cash above that requirement.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized cloud-system spending may escape both earnings and maintenance capex
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.6 million increase in capitalized CCA implementation costs during FY2025, equal to 14.4% of the $212.1 million OE anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: CCA implementation payments reduce OE as cash operating or sustaining investment even though they are recorded in other assets rather than fixed-asset capex; related amortization must not create an unmatched add-back.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 25, 2025 and December 26, 2024, CCA implementation costs included in other assets were $ 38.1 million and $ 7.5 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $30.6 million asset increase but does not establish the cash paid, cash-flow classification, amount included in the OE calculation, sustaining portion, or recurrence. If the OE anchor was derived from operating cash flow, some or all may already be captured; if it used earnings plus add-backs less fixed-asset maintenance capex, it may be omitted. The record therefore identifies a real tracing gap but cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the FY2025 CCA rollforward to cash-flow-statement line items and the OE worksheet, identify amortization added back, and rerun the anchor and forecast for any unmatched cash payments and sustaining CCA spending.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest violates the premise that financing cost remains inside owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 capitalized interest was $5.755 million, 2.7% of the OE anchor; if wholly omitted and recurring, the computed base-case effect is approximately $80.9 million or $0.75 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized cash interest must enter equity-level OE through the capex deduction or a separate financing-cost deduction because it is absent from current interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company capitalizes interest on borrowings during the active construction period of certain capital projects.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the cash-cost amount, but not an OE error: full cash fixed-asset purchases would already include capitalized interest. Even under the conservative assumption that the entire $5.755 million was omitted every year, the linear base-case reduction is only about 2.5% of equity value and would not alter the conclusion that value is below the $50.23 price.
audit_findings.action: Tie cash interest paid, expensed interest, capitalized interest, and fixed-asset cash purchases to the FY2025 OE calculation; correct only any capitalized interest not already included and confirm forecast treatment under the 2026 refinancing.

audit_findings.title: Signed but uncommenced leases create costs absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 undiscounted commitments were $49.1 million, or $0.45 per share and 1.5% of base equity value if deducted in full; the latest 10-Q reports only $17.4 million remaining, or $0.16 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Rent and opening costs from committed new locations should reduce forecast OE supporting growth; existing lease liabilities should not also be deducted from the equity bridge because rent remains in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Future lease payments exclude approximately $ 49.1 million of legally binding minimum lease payments for operating leases signed but not yet commenced.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitments are demonstrated, but their omission from forecast earnings is not. Their disclosed total is undiscounted and spread across lease terms, so treating the entire FY2025 amount as an immediate value reduction is already conservative and still only 1.5% of base value. The latest remaining uncommenced amount is smaller. This cannot change the valuation conclusion independently.
audit_findings.action: Map the FY2025 $49.1 million commitments to leases commenced, cancelled, or still uncommenced by June 2026 and verify that associated rent, pre-opening costs, sales, and margins are included consistently in scenario forecasts.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring purchased-tax-credit benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: exact purchased-credit benefit unquantified; FY2025 filed energy and other tax-credit reductions total $6.137 million, 2.9% of the OE anchor, implying a conservative base-case ceiling of approximately $86.2 million or $0.79 per share if all were removed as recurring anchor income
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring net tax benefit embedded in FY2025 after-tax earnings should be removed from the OE anchor before projection.
audit_findings.evidence: These federal tax credits were purchased at negotiated discounts, resulting in an income tax benefit recorded during the fiscal year ended December 25, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms that discounted transferable credits produced a benefit, but it does not disclose the credits' purchase cost or isolate their net benefit from other credits. Using all $6.137 million of reported tax-credit reductions as a conservative ceiling, rather than only the smaller purchased-credit discount, produces less than a 3% anchor adjustment and would not change the conclusion relative to the $50.23 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the face amount, cash purchase price, accounting entries, and classification of transferable credits; normalize only the net nonrepeatable benefit and rerun the DCF, documenting evidence if comparable purchases are expected to recur.
